text: God made you to move at camel speed, not leopard speed. Slow down.
explanation:
Many people live at full throttle, even trying to read books without reading them, just summaries. They lie down at night but their minds keep racing, like a parked car with the engine left running for weeks. Eventually something breaks. Stress quietly wears down the heart and the body.

God gave us nights to sleep and a day in seven to rest. Even God rested, not because He was tired, but because His work was finished. Jesus told His busy disciples, "Come aside by yourselves… and rest a while." Take a deep breath. Live in the rhythm of grace.

text: When birds moult and grow new feathers, they need extra moisture. In a season of renewal, soak in more of the Word.
explanation:
"Your youth is renewed like the eagle's." Bird keepers know that during moulting, when old feathers drop and new ones grow in, birds need extra water. Gently misting their feathers helps the renewal along.

If you're in a season where your body or spirit feels worn and you're believing God for renewal, that's the time to get more of His Word, not less: "the washing of water by the word." Listen to it, meditate on it and soak in it. Renewal comes with extra moisture.

text: "His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; he shall return to the days of his youth." Job 33 ends: "He restores to man His righteousness."
explanation:
Elihu describes a man wasting away: no appetite, bones sticking out, "his soul draws near the pit." Then: "If there is a messenger for him, a mediator, one among a thousand, to show man His uprightness, then He is gracious to him, and says, 'Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom.'"

That Mediator is Jesus, and that ransom is His blood. Look at what follows: "His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; he shall return to the days of his youth… for He restores to man His righteousness." Hearing that you're righteous in Christ isn't only good for your soul. It renews you.

text: "We were like grasshoppers in our own sight, and so we were in their sight." How you see yourself is how the enemy sees you.
explanation:
Twelve spies saw the same land flowing with milk and honey and the same giants. Ten said, "We are not able… we were like grasshoppers in our own sight, and so we were in their sight." Caleb said, "Let us go up at once and take possession, for we are well able to overcome it."

The facts were the same; the beliefs were different. Ten reports of "nevertheless" melted a nation's heart. Be careful whose report you take in. And see yourself the way God sees you, because the enemy will treat you the way you see yourself.

text: "They are our bread." Joshua and Caleb saw the giants as food. Every challenge you face can make you stronger.
explanation:
The ten fearful spies said the land "devours its inhabitants." Joshua and Caleb turned it around: "Do not fear the people of the land, for they are our bread; their protection has departed from them, and the Lord is with us."

What if the difficult colleague, the chaotic workplace, even the frightening diagnosis is bread for you, something you'll eat and come out stronger? Red lights when you're running late, setbacks you didn't plan for: another piece of bread. With the Lord on your side, you won't be devoured. You'll be nourished.

text: Israel said, "If only we had died in this wilderness!" God replied, "Just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you."
explanation:
"Death and life are in the power of the tongue." We say we're "dying" to see something, "dead tired," or that we're getting old, without thinking. Israel complained they'd rather have died in the wilderness, and that's exactly where that generation ended up.

The spirit of faith is "I believed, therefore I spoke." Fear works the same way in reverse: believing the wrong report, then speaking it. Jesus said, "As you have believed, so let it be done for you." Fill your heart with what God says, and let your words agree with Him.

text: At 80, Barzillai said, "How long have I to live?" At 85, Caleb said, "I am as strong this day as on the day Moses sent me. Give me this mountain."
explanation:
Barzillai was a generous, devoted friend who supplied David in his exile. But when David invited him to the palace, he said he could no longer taste food or hear singing and only wanted to go home and die. His heart was good; his words were full of old age and death.

Caleb, five years older, said, "The Lord has kept me alive… as yet I am as strong this day as on the day that Moses sent me… Now therefore, give me this mountain," a mountain still held by giants. He'd believed God's word for 45 years. Don't let age decide your strength. Let God's promise decide it.
